name: Cylindrical Coordinates (Introduction)
description: Extending polar to 3D: polar in the base, plus height above/below.

content.overview: Picture a soda can. Now picture trying to describe exactly where a specific ant is crawling on it. You'd probably say something like "it's this far from the center pole, facing this direction, and this high up." That's cylindrical coordinates—basically polar coordinates that grew a height axis. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: Cylindrical = (r, θ, z) for describing points in 3D
r = distance from the central vertical axis
θ = angle you've swept around that axis
z = height, same as it would be in Cartesian
Perfect fit for anything with circular symmetry
Basically: polar coordinates, plus a height reading
content.whyItMatters: Rotating systems, vortexes, turbines, drills—cylindrical coordinates make all of them feel almost easy. Try to force one of these problems into plain Cartesian and you'll end up fighting the math the whole way; switch to cylindrical and the circular symmetry just does the work for you.
